cells.remarks: Brāhmanas who are referred to as čhāryas. In characters of the 13th century. Text published in Ins. in N. Kārnāj. ka and Kolhayur State, Ins. No. 37. States that after conquering the entire South and uprooting the Chōđa (i.e., Chōla) dynasty, the conquerer was a creat of the victorious city (vījaya-ka-pata) of Mēlīpāti in order to distribute, among his servants, the Chōđa, Clēra and Sibhalo territories conquered by him, to accept tributes from his feudetories and to arrange for the construction of the Krishṇesvara and Gapđa-mārtītāṇ-Āditya temples in the vicinity of Śetu and the Kālēpriya, Vikaṭachakra and other temples in the Kāñchi-mezđala when he made a grant of the village of Rikkaṭi, situated in Alati ge—700, a sub-division of Nungur-dvishaya, as brāhmadēya; for his parents' and his own merit, to Gōvinda-bhatṭa, son of Ishutta-dēva-bhatṭa. The donee is stated to have heiled from Kurē-grima, a village in Karahāṭa-vishaya and as belonging to the Atrēya-gōtra and Bahvyricha-śākhā. The writer of the charter was Yōddhyamma. Published in JBRAS (New Series), Vol. X. pp. 21 f., and Plate.

cells.remarks: States that on the representation of the Vaḍḷakaramaḷu of Oṇṭimiṭṭa that they were prevented by the Balijas from mounting the car on the day of the car festival of god Tirumala, the chief of the place, while camping at Tirupati, having enquired about the matter and finding the truth in this regard at Tirupati, bestowed upon them (i.e. the Vaḍḷakaramaḷu community of Oṇṭimiṭṭa) the same rights as they had enjoyed from the days of Peda-Tirumala-rāyya. Cf. further Source of Vijayanagara History, Vol. II, p. 368.

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH / CUDDAPAM DISTRICT / SIDDHUVATTAM TALUK · Oṇṭimiṭṭa † — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: Pavement slab in the courtyard, near the haḷēma-maṇḍapa.
cells.remarks: Records the undertaking given by the villagers of Vaṅtimetta to measure out 3½ munitas of ghee every month to the temple of Kōdaṇdarāmasvāmi for a perpetual lamp.

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH / CUDDAPAM DISTRICT / SIDDHUVATTAM TALUK · Oṇṭimiṭṭa † — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: Slab fixed into the wall of the vāyusālā in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records an undertaking given by the Reḍḍis and Kāranams of Sākharājupalle agreeing to give a monthly donation of money (?) for burning a perpetual lamp for god Kōdaṇḍarāmasvāmi. In late characters.

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH / CUDDAPAM DISTRICT / SIDDHUVATTAM TALUK · Oṇṭimiṭṭa † — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: Slab fixed into the wall of the vāyusālā in Kōdaṇḍarāmasvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that the image of the Dvārapālaka was caused to be made by Sidhirāju, son of Vōṇṭimiṭṭa Kāḷappa-rāju. In characters of about the 15th century.

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH / CUDDAPAM DISTRICT / SIDDHUVATTAM TALUK · Oṇṭimiṭṭa † — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: Another Dvārapālaka image to the proper right of entrance.
cells.remarks: Records that the image of Dvārapālaka was caused to be made by the same person mentioned in No. 6 above.

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH / CUDDAPAM DISTRICT / SIDDHUVATTAM TALUK · Hyderabad — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: Salar Jang Museum. Stone image of a Tīrthaṅkara in the ‘South India Room’ (SJM XLI.85). Findspot: Yelburga, Yelburga Taluk, Raichur District.
cells.remarks: States that this image of Pañchaparamēshhi was made by Dēvanna, son of Senabūva Āchanna of Erambarage, a disciple (chatja) of Mādhavachandra-bhattāraka, who belonged to the Mūla-saṅgha, Dēsiya-gana, Pustaka-gachchha and Yimgalētvara-bali. In characters of about the 12th century. Published in Hyd. Arch. Series, No. 12, The Kannada Inscriptions of Kopbal, No. 10 ; Jainism in South India, pp. 381-83.

cells.location: ANDHRA PRADESH / CUDDAPAM DISTRICT / SIDDHUVATTAM TALUK · Hyderabad † — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: Another stone image of a Tīrthaṅkara in the same place. (SJM XLI.72). Findspot: Yelburga, Yelburga Taluk, Raichur District †
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. Records that this of Ēmōyara was made by Koṇḍimayya and his wife Mājave, and the lay disciple of Rājaguru maṇḍalācārya Mādhavacandra-dhānta-cakravarti caused the image of Chauvīśa-tīrthaṅkara i.e. the ‘24 Tīrthaṅkaras’ to be made and presented it to the basadi built by Mādēva-daṇḍanāyaka of Mūla-saṅgha and Drāviḍa gaṇa. Do. ibid., No. 9; Jaina in South India, pp. 379-81.

cells.remarks: Records the grant of lands to provide for curd-rice (dadhy-ōdana) offering and ekanāma worship to god Lakṣmīnarasimhasvāmī by the king. The donor was Māyarta Cāmarasa, namarasa of Agastya-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Ṛik-śākhā. This included the provisions made for the priest, the person serving tulasi and the person who recites the sahasranāma.

cells.place: East wall

cells.location: TERRITORY OF GOA / BICHOLIM TALUK · Tirukkakkari — Goa

cells.date: Regnal year 5+5, Jupiter in Mīna, Mēḍam.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of one perpetual lamp, camphor for burning it and provision for two mid-day meals (oṇam) by Sadiraśikhā-maṇi alias Kīḻaṅṅaḷ. Also records the gift of another lamp by Tamperumāṉiyār (mother?). Specifies the dishes for the meals and the lands set apart to provide for the expense of the above. Published in T.A.S., Vol. II, pp. 169 ff. and Plate.

cells.location: TERRITORY OF GOA / BICHOLIM TALUK · Tirukkakkari † — Goa
cells.place: Maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine, of Mahāviṣṇu temple. base. †
cells.dynasty: Chōḷa †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 40 kālaṇja of gold by Gövindan Kunrap-pōlaṇ of Kuvalāyini for purchasing land to provide for the midday offerings to the god from the day of Pūrādam to Tiruvōnam. The offerings were to be distributed equally, one-half to the brāhmanas and Śrivaishnavas and the other, to the temple servants. Hibd., p. 46 f.

cells.location: TERRITORY OF GOA / BICHOLIM TALUK · Tirukkakkari † — Goa

cells.remarks: Records the arrangement made for supplying ghee to the temple in the months of Mithuna, Karkataka and Sinha by Nārāyappa-Tēvan, Nakkan-Iravi and Ādicchahan-Iravi who were holding the temple lands. Pōjan Kumaran of Pangiturutti, the governor of Nēţumpurma-nādu and Kalkāraikkuñji and two others order the ghee above glace through Nārāyapa-Tēvan. Ibid., p. 42 ff.

cells.place: No. 4

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / GWALIOR (GIRD) DISTRICT / GWALIOR (GIRD) TAHSIL · Gwalior † — Madhya Pradesh
cells.place: No. 5

The order was issued at the instance of Kambai-nādājāyān representing Sāttan Nārāyanan alias Tiruvagattišvarayōgi, of the temple. Noticed in the Topographical List of Travancore Inscriptions, No. 9, cf. Nos. 1, 3 and 12 also.

cells.location: KANYAKUMARI DISTRICT / AGASTHEESVARAN TALUK · KANYAKUMARI DISTRICT / AGASTHEESVARAN TALUK † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same rock
cells.remarks: The lines of the writing run from bottom upwards. Opens with an invocation to the Buddha and gives the mythical genealogy of Pallava, the founder of the Pallava dynasty. Verse 8 gives the popular etymology of the name Pallava. Then are given the names of seven Pallava kings: Mahēndra-varman, his son Bhīmavarmman, his son Siṃhavarman, his son Aṛkavarman, then Uṛavarman, then his son Siṃhavishṇu and lastly Siṃhavarman. The incomplete prose passage at the end states that Siṃhavarman on his return from an expedition to the north, came to a place called Dhānyaghaṭaka or Dhānyaghaṭaka, sacred to the Buddha. Further details are lost, the stone being broken here. In characters of about the 11th century. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. X, pp. 43-44, and Plate and in SII, Vol. I, No. 32.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Kumbakōnam.—Kumbhēšavarasvāmi temple, underground roqm. Stone jamb at the entrance.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Records a grant for providing food-offerings to a deity by Arambaṇadi of Tiyankudippalli of Ii...nādu. The record was written by Pulaiya... ...the permutation of Tiyankuḍi. In characters of the 10th century.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Stone paved into the floor inside the big ... Nandi in Kumbhēśvarasvāmī temple. †
cells.remarks: Very much erased. Purport not clear.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Sōmēšvarasvāmi temple, mahāmandapa, southern entrance, lintel.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Records a grant for food-offerings (pūvu) to god [Sō]mēśvarattu-Mādēvar by Nam[bī]n... alias... Other details are lost. In characters of the 9th-10th century.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Central shrine of Sōmēśvarasvāmī temple, south wall, stone built into it. †
cells.remarks: Do. Records the names of some brāhmaṇas, like Śivan ... Śirīmabhajjaṇ, Vāṇaman Pāla..., Agnichchitan, etc. In characters of about the 12th century A.D.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Chakrapānisvāmi temple, central shrine, south wall.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 120 paṇam for the offering of mṛigānśaṁ to god Tiruvāli-Ālvār and to Bhaṭṭakāraival probably by Kāñchī-kula... The Ālvār who received the offering was later to be distributed to the Srīvaishṇava pilgrims.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Western and southern wall, tiers .
cells.remarks: Records the gift of one silver pitcher and a tiruppudava (grove) to [Kṛishṇa]rāya-nāyakkar by Periya-nāyakkar, son of [Kṛishṇa]rāya-nāyakkar for śīranchakkārippu. In modern characters.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Northern wall, tiers .
cells.remarks: Records that the supply of garlands to god Chakkarapāṇi was the charge of Vēńkaṭa-nāyakkar. Do.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Stone vessel as a step at the entrance into the ma[ṇḍapa] in Chakrapāṇisvāmī temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged and erased. Refers to Chakkapāṇi and Tirumalai-rājapuram. Other details are not clear. In late characters.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Pillar in the madappalī in the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records the gift (ukchayam) of a sandhi-lamp to god Tirukkō... [Sēram-uḍaiyār on ...lugar Oruvan-aḍarkudi] and another lamp by his wife, Namsivāyadēvan Uyyavandāl. In characters of the 13th century.

cells.location: THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBAKONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Two pillars and a cornice in the place of Chakrapāṇisvāmī. †
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Registers the 'receipt of 15 kalam of paddy by the Sivabrāhmaṇas and the Ugachchar of some temple, to provide, out of the interest on the same, for the procession of the deity every year [from the month of Aippasi of a particular year from Tāvalar Alai(Eṭṭaimali)] of Mukundanār, a merchant residing in the maḍaiyālīrs of Gauṇḍakoṇḍālapuram. Do.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBARONAM TALUK · MADRAS—contd / THANJAVUR DISTRICT—concld / KUMBARONAM TALUK—concld — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Kumbakönam—concld.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / KUMBARONAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Prākāra around the central shrine, stone built into the northern (outer) wall.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of Vāṇḍāyavan-tiruvīdi to provide for the daily offerings to god Tiruvāli-Ālvār of Chakkara-tīrtham in Tirukkudandai, by Aļavār-Vīrarāghavan of Perumbadūr. Mentions Tepperumānallūrvāykkāl and the river Kāvēri among the boundaries. In modern characters.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · PAPANASAM TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Chakkarüppalji (Ayyumpöštai).—Chakravähésvara temple, central shrine, south wall and tiers.
cells.remarks: Records the sale of land made tax-free to god Sürya-děvar for whom a temple was built in Ckakkarappalji by Ādittañ Süryañ ulias Chembiyan of Veštakkudji, the kiļuvañ of Po[j*]jgi-nādū, by the sabhaiyār Agalimañgalam, a brahma-dēyam in Kilār-kürram. The land endowed is stated to have been rendered fallow by the breaching of the banks of Kåvéri to the west of the temple at Tiruchehakkarappalji in the 5th year of king Rājakčsari, who died in the golden palace (poṇmāļigaittuñjiṇa). In characters of the 10th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Kumbakōṇam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: To the proper right of No. 308 above on the wall of Chakravāhēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Records the exemption from taxes of several pieces of land belonging to god Mahādēvar of Tiruchchakkarappalli receiving money in lieu from the temple itself by the sabhaiyār of Agaliyamangalam, a brāhmaṇadēyam in Kīlār-kūrram in Nittavinōda-vaḷanāḍu. The sabhaiyār also agree to have met in front of the Gaṇapatyār shrine in the temple.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Kīlkoḷippaṭṭu — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Bālakāṇḍa temple, jamb left of entrance into the mahā-maṇḍapa in front of the Śiva shrine.
cells.date: Šaka 1656, Kali 4835, Ānan la, Āvaṇi 29, šu. 12, Friday=1734 A.D., August 30.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the central shrine, ardhamandapa mahīmandapa, nrityamandapa. pråtara and göpura and the consecration of parivāradžvalaiga for Bhūmināthar and Bhūlōkanāyakiyammañ in Bhūmipuram by Ševattu-cheštiyār of the Talaikkudai-mahārishi götram.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Kīlkoḷippaṭṭu † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Amman shrine, left of entrance into the ardhamandapa.
cells.date: Šaka 1656, Kali 4835, Ānan la, Āvaṇi 29, šu. 12, Friday=1734 A.D., August 30.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to be another version of No. 310 above.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Kīlkoḷippaṭṭu † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Stone set up near the western entrance of the temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1639, Kali 4818, Hēviḷambi, Āvaṇi 6, Wednesday=1717 A.D., April 3.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of land for maintaining a chaṭṭiram built by the Garuṇatha-cheṭṭiyār in Māṇmevādi by some members of the community called Tiraikkuṇḍār.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Neḍuvāśal — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Aruṇāchalēśvara temple, entrance, ceiling, four inscribed stones.
cells.remarks: Each one of the inscriptions states that this stone (i.e. one on which it is engraved) was contributed by Vīrappachcheṭṭiyār, Tiruvāḍu-uḍai-cheṭṭi, Muthu and Karuppacheṭṭi respectively. In late characters.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Neḍuvāśal † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Step-stone at the entrance into the manḍapa in front of the central shrine.
cells.remarks: Mentions Suppiramaṇiyan, son of Chellappa-mudaḷiyār as the donor. Do.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Śiṇṇamaṇai — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: (Ruins of Kurikaiayal).— Chidambarēśvara temple, central shrine, some disconnected fragments built into the walls.
cells.remarks: Seems to record the rates of levy on merchandise like betelnuts, cotton, pepper etc. at the port. One of the fragments mentions regnal year 34. In characters of about the 14th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Śiṇṇamaṇai † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: North wall of Chidambarēśvara temple. First tier. †
cells.remarks: Records the obeisance of one Riammasēṭṭi Tittār. In late characters.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Muśiri — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Stone built into the side of steps on the river-side.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. States that the steps on the river-side were caused to be constructed by the son of Līngama-nāyakkar.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Muśiri † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Chandramaulīśvara temple, ardhamāṇḍapa, pillar.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of income from certain levies from the residents of a locality to Chōḷēśvaramuḍaiya-nāyaṉār in Muśiri alias Mummuḍiśōḷa-pēṭṭai in Āmūr-nāḍu in Rājēndra-vaḷanāḍu by Muḷvāy Viṉaiya-deṉāyakkar. Mentions Dūvargal Kumāra Vīraṇṇar-aṇṇar and adhikāri Tiruvōṅgulam-uḍaiya Chōḷappērumāḷ. In late characters.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Kuraṅgāthēśvara temple, central shrine, south wall.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Appears to record the sale of land by the Mūlaparaḍaiyār (of a village, name lost) to the temple of Tirukkuraṅgāthēśvara-uḍaiya-mahādēvar for the purpose of burning a lamp, been formerly endowed by a person (name lost) of Kīlār-nāḍu and his dēviyār Naṅgai Kūrrapperumā... for burning four lamps in the temple. In characters of about the 10th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: North wall
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Appears to record a gift of land, made tax-free, by the Mūlc-pe re daiyār to the temple of Tirukkura-kkutturaip-porumānadīgaĵ. Refers to six brāhmanas including Naĵa-Nārīyananān Ādittepiqāran. Do.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: East wall
cells.remarks: Records the name Sammaĵa Komāpappa. In characters of about the 14th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Višvanātha temple, outer prākāra, west wall.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. The king bears the chain of titles bhāshatikut-tarpuverāye ragc uđa etc., of the Vijsyanagara kings. Portion after the date is lost.

cells.location: MADRAS / THANJAVUR DISTRICT / PAPANASAM TALUK — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: East wall
cells.remarks: Consists of five fragments of which one appears to record a gift of land for burning a lamp in a temple and two refer to a gift of land by purchase for raising a flower gurden. In characters of about the 13th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · MADRAS—contd / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT—contd / MUSIRI TALUK—concld — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Śrínivāsanallūr—concld.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: East wall
cells.remarks: Consists of three fragments recording gifts of tax-free lands to a temple for purposes like burning incense (tiruchpugai). Contains references to Alagiyamanavājap-perunā, Kērajavalanādu, Śri Hanumān and Sōja-Kumarapālan. In characters of the 12th-13th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Slabs built in different places in Kuraṅgāthēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Consists of fragments referring to the sale of oykkaiyar for 127 kāśu and mentions the wife of a brāhmaṇa (brāhmaṇi) called Kaupiyan Nārāyaṇan Singan. In characters of about the 10th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Rāmanātha temple, central shrine, maṇdapa in front, north and east walls (inside).
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Contains portions of the king's praśasti, Pugaļindha yuvani etc. Refers to one Tiruvaranga Māḷaśar, a committee (vāriyam) member, and a grant of land. Probably same as SII, Vol. VIII, No. 608-A of 1904. Published in SII, Vol. XVIII, No. 660, (p. 302).

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Fragments built in different places in Rāmanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Consists of five pieces probably recording the exemption from taxes of some land granted by the village of Jayangondaśōla-chaturvēdimangalam to some individuals, (now) old by purchase for the bathing (ēkādaśi-tirrumañjanam) of a deity (name lost) on the day of Viśākham in the month of Ani. In characters of about the 11th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: North of entrance, east wall, outside of Rāmanātha temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Refers to the grant of five oṇrādu-narkālu for the payment of taxes (śīraikkāśu) in connection with some land. In characters of about the 12th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Tiruvēṅgimalni — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Maraged-dāchalcś vara temple, ardha-maṇdapa, south wall.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of (tirumun eykkādu) perpetually on the occasion of food-offering to the authorities of the temple of Tiruvāgīśu-rāmuḍaiyār to Nāyakan-uḍaiyār alias Tirniruppallavarāyan.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: South wall, tiers
cells.date: Regnal year 31, Vrischika śu. 6, Avittam, Saturday, = 1208, November 15.
cells.remarks: Registers the deed pertaining to the sale of land in Alagarakōyil Kulttunga-rājamallar-lattaisai for 300 oṇrādu narkālu to Uyyavandaiyār of Uraiyur, a merchant in Rājasēndra-śōja-pēttai by the mahāsabhaiyār of Jayangonda-śōlanallur to go towards the expenses of food offerings (taligai) and worship as dēnadānam to god Subramanya-pillaiyār whose image was set up in the temple of Tiruvāgīgöy-uḍaiyār by the merchant.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: South wall
cells.date: Regnal year 16, Kumbha śu. 10, Rohiṇī, Monday, 1162 A.D., January 27, f.d.t. .89 and d.n. .02.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of land by Alagiyān Mēy-Vēḷākkēppaaḷavarayan, one of the cōḻa mudalis of Chattan- Cheṭṭirāyan for the latter's well being to god Subrahmanyēśvaramuḍaiya-nāyaṉār in the northern part of 'Jayaṅgoṇḍaśōḷa-chaturppēdimangalam for worship, offerings, the agence and other special occasions. The land is said to have been purchased by the donor from Tirunaṭṭappuśīlas Tirukkaliṟṟuppaḍi-nambi.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: North wall, tiers
cells.date: Regnal year 39, Rishabha śu. 3, Magham, Monday, Irregular.
cells.remarks: Registers a similar deed as in No. 330 above pertaining to the sale of land in Kulōttunga āļanallūr-lesttalai for 100 current good kāšu to Uyyaninrāduvān Viļumiyār of Pungapūr in Tiruvāli-nādu by the Perunguri malācc-lhciyāt of Jeyan-gondaśōļach-chaturvēdimargalam in Mimalai for being endowed for worship and offerings to Ājudaiya-piļaiyār, Tirunāvukkaraṇdēvar, Ālālasunderepperumā erd Tirunarkira-dēvar whose images were set up in the same temple by Viļumiyār.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Mahāmaṇḍapa, south wall, tiers
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Seems to record the royal grant of tax-free lands to the bhajas of Agaram Mādhavachaturvēdimaṅgalam said to have been created by and named after the king. Notturuḍaiyāṉ Kāḷigāryar figures as the signatory. In characters of the 14th century.

cells.location: MADRAS / TIRUCHCHIRAPPALLI DISTRICT / MUSIRI TALUK · Śrīnivāsanallūr † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Vināyaka shrine, south wall, tiers
cells.date:
Regnal year 7, Simha šu. 15, Sadaiyam, Tuesday =
1249 A. D., August 24, or 1252 A.D., August 20.
cells.remarks: Records the sale of land by auction by the authorities of the temple of Tiruvāḍuturai-uḍaiya-mahādēvar to Tiru-vīra- Eṇṇāḍuḍaiyāṉ alias Puṇṇiyavāṉ-cheṭṭi, a merchant of Chōḷapuram, having received 2500 paṇam nārā kāsū from the latter. The Dēvarkkaṇṇi-paḷ exempted the land from its liability to pay the taxes. The land was apart for the maintenance of the persons looking after the tank until the well dug by the merchant.

cells.place: Another-sluice-stone near by.
cells.remarks: States that the Sundara-Pāṇḍya-yī-ēri was caused to be constructed in Veṇṇāḍu-uḍaiya Sundarapāṇḍya-ccaturvēdimangalam in Jīṉi-nāḍu by Nambi Poḍuvaṉ alias Poṉ Eṉai Kōḍiyēru in Malai-maṇḍalam. In characters of the 13th century.

cells.remarks: Bilingual. Seems to record the construction of the bastion called Buruja Hajarate Divāna Ālāmūrtājā Śāhī by Ahamadā Āgā. In characters of the 16th century. For the Persian portion, see Appendix D, No. 191.

The grants were received by Ananta-viryya-Siddhānta-muniśvara of Yāpaniya saṅgha and Kandūr gaṇa.

cells.remarks: Records a grant of land for offerings to god Hadavalēśvara after laying the foot of Vāvēśvara-paṇḍita, the disciple of Vāmadēva-paṇḍita, known as Ēkōcchārakaravarti, the son of Sōmidēva, a scion of Vāyambhudeva of Muḷugunda and Heggade Kāvaṇa, śāsana-kāra. The gift was made by the Nāyakka and ruler of Noḷukunda situated in Māvaḷe-500. Kāvāṇa is stated to be the subordinate of Daṇḍanāyaka Mādirājayya, the administrator of Tammayūru-Pannir-ppalli, Mūḷu-Kōḍe, Kiruvatti, Kaggavige, Ammaṇagaypbhāvi and Nilagunda. Also records the gift of the king, Ēśvara Vīra Permāḍi, the son of Kadamba. Jayakēśi II and Maialadēvi, and ruler of Koṃkaṇa-900, Palāśige-12,000 and Kavadiḍvīpasvālakka. Also records the gift of a garden by the merchants probably to the same deity. Mentions Dāśimayya-paṇḍita-paṇḍita, the disciple Vāvēśvara-paṇḍita and further records grant of land by the merchant, Mārōja.

Records that Hākiballadēva’s minister Bammachayya caused to be constructed a Jaina temple and also made grants of land and an oil mill for services to the deity Śāntināthadēva installed therein, and for the feeding of Jaina ascetics. Gives the pedigree of Malladēva. The record was composed by Tradi (Tīrvādi) Vāchhā. Madha(dhu)jandārayaka of the Sōḍhalā family was the engraver. New Indian Antiquary, Vol. II, pp. 34 ff. Sāthāka died in this battle and his wife named Paṭasā (?) probably committed saff. Published in ibid., p. 41.

cells.remarks: Late. Records the construction of a śēpa, a well, a charitable water-stall (prapā), and a garden (ārāma) by Dattabhaṭa, who is described as the commander of the army of the ruler and the son of Vāyurakshita who in turn was the commander of the Gupta emperor Gōvindagupta, son of Chandragupta. The composer was Ravila. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXVII, pp. 12-18, and Plate.

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / GWALIOR (GIRD) DISTRICT / GWALIOR TAHSIL · Jabalpur District, Murwara Tahsil. Bargaon — Madhya Pradesh

cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seems to record the gift of cess on the threshing floor (khala-bhikshā) together with granary (kōshṭha) to one residing in the temple to the settlement of brāhmaṇas for the benefit of god Saṅkarshaṇārāyaṇa. Mentions a certain Śabara. Is datable to about the 10th century. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXV, pp. 278-81; and C.I.I., Vol. IV, pp. 195-98, and Plate XXXIII.

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / GWALIOR (GIRD) DISTRICT / GWALIOR TAHSIL · Morena District, Seopur Tahsil. Dubkunda — Madhya Pradesh
cells.place: Stone slab lying in the ruins of a temple.
cells.date: Vikrama 1145, Bhādrapada śu. 3, Monday=1088 A.D., August 21.
cells.remarks: In two parts. The first part gives an account of the genealogy of the king, while the second records the foundation of a temple by the king and the grant of a village named Viniōpāka (i.e., a tax) on each gōṇī (gunny bag of grain?) and the gift of a piece of land in the village of Mahāchakra capable of being sown with four gōṇīs of wheat and a garden with a well to the temple of Śiva built by the king for the purpose of the construction of the temple and for keeping it in good repair as well as for worship there. Also states that the king made provision of oil for lamps and for anointing the bodies of holy men. The composer of the prasasti was Udayanija and its engraver was Tilhaṇa. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. II, pp. 232 ff.

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / GWALIOR (GIRD) DISTRICT / GWALIOR TAHSIL · Fatehpur — Madhya Pradesh

Mentions the names of officials like Bhāusāheba. The mason was Uvata śyōkisana (i.e., śivakṛiṣhṇa).

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / MORENA DISTRICT / SGOPUR TAHSIL · Raipurā — Madhya Pradesh

Also records the construction of a temple by śivānātha and others, when Uttamarāma, son of Indrasiṁha was ruling over Gadha Raṇathambhora a śūbā (sub-division) of Ajmer. The mason was śhēmā (Khēmā).

cells.location: MADHYA PRADESH / MORENA DISTRICT / SGOPUR TAHSIL — Madhya Pradesh

cells.remarks: Trilingual. States that Tīr Ārākel, son of Pūghū of Julfā (in īrān), the pricet (pādrī) of the Armenian Christians who used to live in the Church of Shāwāli came, by chance, to Narwar in India on the first date and after staying there for 10 years died on the second date at the age of 72, and that his sons after having kept his body for six months in this grave, carried it to the Hoog(h)ly-Bandar (near Calcutta). The chronogram gives the date of the death of the Qāḍī and Makānī (sic), i.e. emperor Jahāngīr. Date that of writing (?). Cf. Ind. His. Quar., vol. III, No. 4 (1927), pp. 715-18, plate.

Also states that whoever renders help in this regard, Ḥaḍrat Mīṭhe Shāh will have his desires fulfilled. Further mentions Shaikh Fīroz, one of the servants of the (said) Khān Ṣāḥib and deputy (in charge) of the fort (nā'ib-i-qal'a), as the supervisor.

cells.location: RAJASTHAN / KOTA DISTRICT / SANGOD TAUSIL / SHAHABAD TAHSIL · Loose slab in the Tahsil office — Rajasthan
cells.place: Originally from a platform near the KotwālǮ.
cells.date: Regnal Year 23 (A. H. 1090), Ramadān 14=1679 A.D., October 9.
cells.remarks: Bilingual. Fragmentary. States that the maḥājans, traders and Brahmins of the gegāra (pargana) made a representation to the emperor that the levy on on landed property (ǫāgīr) was being recovered, a royal decree (faqīr decree) was issued under the orders of the emperor laying down that the levy was illegal and should not be taken. It also states that, in pursuance of that order, the faujdār Ībn-i-Raiṣān Khān (also designated as ‘āmgīrniṣīn) to stop levying those imposts, and as a result, (the amount of the levy) like ḿāṣā, baṣā', ḿātā, khonā', tolā, kotwalī, etc., half was remitted and the remaining half, being accepted by the concerned on their free-will, is to be well, while the taxes on butchers and wine-sellers were totally remitted, in accordance with a curse of 'Alīl and Rām for the Muslim or Hindu violators. For the Nāgarī portion, see No. 247 of Appendix B of A. R. Ep., 1966-67.

(2) A. H. 1119 (words) = 1707-08 A. D.
cells.remarks: Records the following incident: the late Nawwāb, Mirzā 'Āshūr Baig, entitled Āghar Khān, having started from Kābul for India in compliance with the orders of omperor 'Ālamgīr reached Sarāi Jājhau on the first date. Having learnt that only two days before his arrival, a group of Sayyids who were going on pilgrimage (to Mecca) was waylaid by the infidels who looted them and also made them captives, the religious-minded Nawwāb attacked and burnt the villages of the infidels, killed many of them and released the Muslim prisoners, but himself attained martyrdom. On the second date, his son, Mughal, who was endowed with the hereditary title, inscribed the tablet with his own hand. quoting a few verses composed by Mīr Huwaidā Balkhi on the martyrdom of his father. Cf. Proc. As. Soc. Beng., 1874, pp. 165-06.
